title: Heracles: Strong Man or Problem?
subtitle: The hero who also wrecks things — weighing the ledger

learningObjectives.text: Why is Heracles both saviour and problem?
What is he actually FOR in the myths?

narrativeBlocks.title: The civilizing strong man
narrativeBlocks.body: On one side: he clears the world of monsters, frees Prometheus, kills bandits on every road, breaks the death-god's hold on Alcestis. He is the great remover — whatever is too dangerous for everyone else, he does.

narrativeBlocks.title: And the wrecker
narrativeBlocks.body: On the other side: he sacks cities on slight provocation, kills a guest-friend (Iphitus) in a rage, fights the god Apollo for a tripod, nearly breaks hospitality rules everywhere he goes. The same body that saves also smashes.

narrativeBlocks.title: A god's appetite
narrativeBlocks.body: Heracles eats like a force of nature and loves like a disaster — dozens of liaisons, a trail of sons across the Greek world. He is civilization's patron AND its problem, depending on which side of him you land.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why keep both halves?
narrativeBlocks.body: The myths don't reconcile the contradiction — they preserve it. Heracles is the honest hero: the strength that protects is the same strength that harms, and you don't get one without the other.

narrativeBlocks.title: The ancestor of the strong hero
narrativeBlocks.body: Every strong-with-questions hero that follows — Beowulf, Samson, the Hulk — runs on the Heracles template: power enormous enough to solve anything, and dangerous enough to be the problem itself.

quiz.prompt: Why is Heracles a 'problem' as well as a saviour?

choices.text: The same strength that clears monsters also sacks cities and breaks hospitality — the myths keep both halves
He serves King Arcesilaus in exile as penance
He refuses to fight at all

quiz.explanation: Heracles is the honest hero: protector and destroyer are the same quality at different moments.

quiz.prompt: What role does Heracles play in the mythological world?

choices.text: The great remover — he handles the dangers no one else can, and his power is what makes him both indispensable and dangerous
A villain the other heroes must stop

quiz.explanation: The Greeks made him the answer to any impossible problem — and the question of what such power costs.
